text:
carla: Hey team, customer reported a spike of 401s hitting our service-proxy right after we rotated the API key this morning. They rotated key via Vault and KMS rewrap succeeded but clients see 401.

maria: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the curl + proxy log snippet you see? Which customer/org?

carla: org: acme-inc, repro curl: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <new-key>" https://proxy.redwood.ai/v1/predict
* Connected to proxy.redwood.ai
< HTTP/2 401
{"error":"Unauthorized","reason":"key not found"}
```
proxy log: `auth: key lookup failed for kid=abc123, returned not_found`

jordan: Two quick checks: 1) confirm Vault kv path and version (kv v1 vs v2) 2) check how proxy gets secret (env var, file, sidecar CSI).

carla: We wrote new key to `vault kv put secret/services/proxy/keys acme=...` and rewrapped through KMS (logs show rewrap-ok). Our helm values were updated but pods still show old env: `KEY=ey..old` inside container.

evans: Could be a gitops/operator race — if the Git commit with old values was re-applied it can snap back secrets. Check Argo/Flux events and helm history: `helm history proxy --kube-namespace svc-acme`.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: GitOps: observed automated rollback of helm release `proxy` to revision 42 by gitops-bot at 2026-03-16T09:11:02Z

jen: Also check CDN/edge caches — if signed tokens are cached at the edge a client can reuse an old token and then fail when our origin rejects it. But here origin says kid not found so origin key mismatch.

carla: Confirmed: `kubectl exec -n svc-acme deploy/proxy -- cat /etc/secrets/proxy.key` -> shows old key contents. CSI driver is used to mount the secret. The CSI logs show no update event since rotation.

jordan: CSI driver might not be configured to watch Vault secret versions or secretRefresh may be disabled. For a quick fix: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/proxy -n svc-acme` or delete pods to force mount refresh. Also check the secret controller: `kubectl get secret proxy-keys -n svc-acme -o yaml` to see if k8s secret was updated.

carla: Did `kubectl rollout restart` — pods came up but logs still show old key immediately after start. Then saw `helm release` rollback from deploy-bot above. Looks like gitops pulled a branch with old helm values and re-applied the older secret, overwriting the updated Kubernetes secret.

evans: Root cause likely: rotation write -> updated k8s secret -> some CI job/merge triggered a sync from git and reapplied old secret YAML (helm values encoded) re-creating old secret. That + kube secret mounting semantics caused containers to see old key. Fix path: ensure rotation updates are captured back into gitops or block gitops sync until rotation completes.

jen: Immediate remediation steps we used here: 1) pause gitops sync for proxy (ArgoCD pause) 2) write the rotated key into the helm values commit in a safe repo (or reference Vault directly) 3) `kubectl delete pod -l app=proxy -n svc-acme` to force fresh mounts 4) purge edge cache.

carla: After pausing gitops and re-applying the correct secret and deleting pods, calls now succeed: `curl ...` returns HTTP/200 and predict payload. Logs show `auth: key ok kid=xyz789`.

jordan: Add dev tasks: - ensure rotation job creates a follow-up commit to gitops (or flag) - add a lock/annotation so gitops doesn't reapply during rotation - add detection alert when secret version != mounted version.

evans: Recommend also adding post-rotation hook to invalidate CDN cache and send `kubectl rollout status` checks before unpausing sync. Example post-hook snippet:
```
# after writing secret to Vault
kubectl -n svc-acme set env deployment/proxy ROTATION_BUMP=$(date +%s)
# invalidate edge
curl -X POST https://edge.redwood.ai/invalidate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $EDGE_ADMIN' -d '{"paths":["/v1/*"]}'
```

carla: Thanks — will add notes to the ticket. Customer patch confirmed.

maria: Summary for record: cause = gitops reapply of old helm values overwrote rotated key in k8s secrets -> mounted secret stale in CSI -> auth mismatched -> 401s. Fix = pause sync, write correct secret, restart pods, invalidate edge. Follow-ups: create a rotation runbook, add a gitops lock mechanism, add secret-mount/version mismatch alerting, and add a short grace window for rotation TTL to avoid ~30s races. Assign to eng-infra. :thumbsup:

jen: I'll open ENGINFRA-1124 and add playbook steps + runbook link.

carla: marking as resolved with customer. Closing loop. :white_check_mark:
